title: Full Factorization of a Quintic and Its Standard Zeros
originalTopic: Zeros of a polynomial and the window that shows them all
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Factor f(x) = x^5 - 5x^3 + 4x completely and list all its zeros. Then recommend a window that displays every crossing together with all four turning points.

steps.title: Factor step by step
steps.explanation: Taking out the common factor x leaves a quadratic in x^2, which factors into (x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 4) and then into (x - 1)(x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 2).
steps.why: Complete factorization makes every root visible by inspection instead of relying on a solver's decimal output.

steps.title: List the zeros
steps.explanation: Five real zeros, all simple, so the graph crosses the axis at each one rather than bouncing.
steps.why: Simple roots cross and double roots touch, so multiplicity predicts the local shape at each intercept.

steps.title: Size the vertical span from the turning points
steps.explanation: The largest excursion reached between the zeros is about f(1.705) approx -3.55 and f(0.303) approx 1.08, so nothing of interest exceeds |y| = 4.
steps.why: Bounding the interior extrema is what lets you clip the y-range usefully instead of showing the huge values of the end behavior.

steps.title: State the window
steps.explanation: The x-range covers the outermost zeros with margin and the y-range comfortably contains every turning point, so all five crossings and four humps appear at once.
steps.why: An all-roots window must trade end behavior for interior detail, since a quintic reaches enormous values within a few units of the last root.
